images.seen: A gloved hand holding a hot chocolate with marshmallows on a balcony at sunset, snow on Table Mountain and the Twelve Apostles across the bay, blanket on the lap. Friday.
lines: Hot chocolate has been promoted to equipment tonight, and the view earned it.
Cape Town got Alps for one evening and the whole city is out on balconies.
The mountain wears white maybe twice a winter, and tonight is one of them.

images.seen: A man on his wet doorstep at night under a starry sky, mug in hand, breath steaming in the porch light. Wednesday.
lines: His breath is making better clouds than the sky managed all day.
Clear night, wet steps, visible breath: the frost is filling in its paperwork.
One last look at a sky that is about to get seriously cold.

images.seen: A woman working late at her desk wrapped in a blanket, fingerless gloves on the keyboard, a hot water bottle in a knitted cover hanging on the chair, black night in the window. Thursday.
lines: Fingerless gloves at a laptop: winter has entered the home office.
The house has one warm room after dark, and it is wherever the blanket is.
Hot water bottle is the real MVP today.

images.seen: A couple wrapped in one blanket on a log beside a campfire, tent and camp chairs around them, the Milky Way huge over the Karoo. Friday.
lines: A Karoo night trades warmth for stars, and they took the deal.
The fire handles the front; the blanket handles the back; the sky handles everything else.
Cold enough to share one blanket, clear enough to make it worth it.
